standfirst: Tilapia lake virus, the only member of the family Amnoonviridae. Ten segments, each carrying one ORF, plus an eleventh protein translated from a second reading frame of segment 9 that no sequence database holds. This module is the inverse of the usual LowVan story: the source vocabulary is not sprawling but empty — 363 of 399 distinct deposits are annotated hypothetical protein — so the work was not collapsing names but supplying them.

modules.Tilapinevirus: Eleven features over ten segments. Segments 1–3 form a heterotrimeric orthomyxovirus-like polymerase (PB1, PB2-like, PA-like) by cryo-EM (PMID 38066000); segment 4 is the nucleoprotein (PMID 35107373, PMID 39995042). Segments 5–10 have no assigned function and are declared as uncharacterized lineage-specific proteins under the literature's own S5…S10 designations. Binning is by homology to the Til-4-2011 reference segment set, not by annotation string, because the string separates exactly one protein of eleven.

gaps: Three mechanisms an orthomyxo-like virus might plausibly use are probed for and come back ABSENT, which is the required result: PMID 41513822 searched for splicing, a PA-X-like frameshift and a matrix protein and reports none. S9-F3 arises by leaky ribosomal scanning of an alternative frame, not by splicing. Eleven further amnoonvirid species — Flavolineata, Piscibus, Lipesoluc and the Catfish, Cod, Flatfish, Loach, Lizard (×2) and Pufferfish amnoonviruses — deposit one segment each, PB1 only, and none routes to this module at the annotator's 150-bit floor. They are a documented gap, not a silent omission.
derived: No mature peptides are declared. A cleavable signal peptide is predicted for S5 and, with lower confidence, for S6, but neither is experimentally confirmed and no mature N-terminus has been determined for any amnoonvirid, so no _SP or _MAT product is declared. Declaring one would mean inventing its boundary.

why.S9_F3: The eleventh protein, and BV-BRC holds none of it. PMID 41513822 identified a 105-codon ORF in frame 3 of segment 9, overlapping the 116-codon primary S9 ORF, confirmed by mass spectrometry with 4 unique peptides and 49% sequence coverage, and carrying a CRM1-dependent nuclear export signal. The collection was extracted from the genomes' own segment 9: 32 extractions, every one exactly 105 aa, 82.9–100% pairwise identity, and all 32 sharing the identical N-terminus MDRKYRFCVSNLDR. It is annotated as uncharacterized rather than as a nuclear export protein because the function rests on a single citation no curator here has read, and because calling it NEP would assert equivalence with the influenza protein of that name, which is a spliced product.
why.S3_PA: The diagnostic RT-PCR target for TiLV, which dominates its deposits: 151 of 546 in-scope contigs are segment 3, and 71 of its protein deposits are amplicon translations rather than whole proteins. They were excluded by the length window and the exclusion was then checked structurally rather than assumed — 0 of 71 begin at reference residue 1, and 58 of 71 begin at reference residues 100–124, one primer site, at 98.7% median identity.
why.S5: The only TiLV protein with a predicted transmembrane domain, and the only one for which any structural role has been suggested: PMID 41513822 notes a predicted signal peptide, N-glycosylation sites and a TMD and suggests it “may play a role in the viral envelope structure”. That is a prediction and nothing more — no S5 peptides were detected by mass spectrometry — so the annotation stays uncharacterized.
